sources.title: D. Tong, Kinetic Theory (University of Cambridge Part III lecture notes), Chapter 4 'Linear Response' (separately hosted chapter PDF)
sources.locator: Chapter 4, §4.1.1 'Linear Response' (printed pp. 79-82), §4.1.2 'Analyticity and Causality' (pp. 82-83) and §4.1.3 'Kramers-Kronig Relation' (pp. 83-86) read in full from the 24-page chapter PDF; §4.2 'Classical Examples', §4.3 'Quantum Mechanics and the Kubo Formula' and §4.4 'Response in Quantum Field Theory' (pp. 86-102) inspected for the disposition rows. The printed page numbers are those shown in the document.

contents.name: §4.1.1 Linear Response (pp. 79-82): response function χ(t−t') in the linear relation δ⟨O⟩(t)=∫dt' χ(t−t')φ(t') (4.4), time-translation invariance, Fourier convention f(ω)=∫dt e^{iωt}f(t) (4.5), and the frequency-space response relation (4.6)
contents.support: Supports the transfer-function construction of the consumer's clauses (a)-(c): the pair's kernel K and its transform χ(z)=∫_0^∞K(s)e^{izs}ds are exactly this response function written for a causal matrix kernel; the consumer states the same convolution and its bound as pure mathematics, with no physical interpretation.

contents.name: §4.1.2 Analyticity and Causality (pp. 82-83): the imaginary part as the anti-Hermitian part χ''=−(i/2)(χ−χ*) (4.7), causality χ(t)=0 for t<0, and the contour-completion argument giving analyticity of χ(ω) for Im ω>0
contents.support: Supports the consumer's clause (c) (holomorphy of the transform on the upper half-plane as the analytic content of causality of the kernel) and clause (d) (the Hermitian part (χ−χ*)/(2i) whose nonnegativity is the passivity condition).

contents.name: §4.1.3 Kramers-Kronig Relation (pp. 83-86): the Plemelj-type discontinuity (4.8)-(4.11) of 1/(ω'−ω) with the principal value, the indented upper-half-plane contour closed at infinity under the stated decay assumption (p. 85), the relation χ(ω)=(1/(iπ))P∫χ(ω')/(ω'−ω)dω' (4.13), the real/imaginary pair (4.14)-(4.15) and the reconstruction formula (4.18)
contents.support: This is the same indented-contour route the consumer's clauses (b)-(c) execute with exact hypotheses: the consumer replaces the source's decay assumption by the explicit compact-support bound |χ|≤||K''||_1|z|^{-2} and by the integrable-branch bound |χ|≤(|K(0)|+||K'||_1)/|z|, and proves the principal-value formulas for each matrix entry.

contents.name: §4.2 Classical Examples (damped harmonic oscillator, dissipation, hydrodynamic response), §4.3 Quantum Mechanics and the Kubo Formula (including dissipation again and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem), §4.4 Response in Quantum Field Theory (pp. 86-102)
contents.reason: These sections concern specific classical and quantum models (oscillator, hydrodynamics, Kubo formalism, fluctuation-dissipation) that no item of this pair or of this run's planned pages consumes; the pair's items are pure mathematics about real matrix kernels and their holomorphic transforms, and no claim here is weakened by declining these model applications.

sources.title: D. Tong, Electromagnetism (University of Cambridge lecture notes)
sources.locator: §6.1 'Retarded Potentials' (printed pp. 134-142: Green's function for the Helmholtz equation, Green's function for the wave equation, the retarded potential integrals and the Lorentz-gauge check), §6.2 'Dipole Radiation' (pp. 143-149: electric dipole radiation, power radiated/Larmor formula with application, magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole radiation) and §7.5.4 'Causality and the Kramers-Kronig Relation' (pp. 200-203) read in full; §6.4 'Radiation From a Single Particle' (pp. 157-171) inspected for the disposition row.

contents.name: §6.1 Retarded Potentials (pp. 134-142): Green's function of the wave equation, the retarded scalar and vector potentials as the 1/(4πR) integrals of the source at the retarded time, and the gauge check
contents.support: Supports clause (a) of the consumer: the retarded-potential integrals φ=(μ0c²/4π)∫ρ(·,t−R/c)/R and A=(μ0/4π)∫J(·,t−R/c)/R are exactly the objects defined there (the source's conventions are SI), and the source's Green's-function derivation is the physical counterpart of the consumer's identification of the integrals with the zero-data wave Cauchy solution.

contents.name: §6.2.1-§6.2.2 Electric dipole radiation and power radiated (pp. 143-146): the far-zone 1/r electric and magnetic fields of an oscillating dipole, the Poynting flux and the radiated power (Larmor formula)
contents.support: Supports the far-zone form and the outward-flux limit of the consumer's clauses (b)-(c) in the dipole specialization: the source derives the 1/r transverse fields and the constant-in-r flux integral. The consumer proves the general uniform asymptotic form and the retarded-time flux limit for arbitrary smooth compact conserved sources, of which this is the leading specialization; the dipole power coefficient itself is a physics-layer statement recorded as a deferred destination below.

contents.name: §6.2.4 Magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole radiation (p. 149)
contents.reason: The approved radiation inventory proves controlled leading electric-dipole radiation with its exact absolute remainders, plus exact point fields/powers. This source-specific next-order magnetic-dipole/electric-quadrupole radiation expansion is not a promised branch or a conclusion of the electric-dipole theorem. All approved leading and exact radiation claims remain intact.

contents.name: §6.4 Radiation from a single particle (Li ́enard-Wiechert potentials, fields of an accelerated point charge, covariant formulation and synchrotron radiation, pp. 157-171)
contents.reason: Point-particle radiation uses the retarded root of |x−z(s)|=c(t−s), the Li ́enard-Wiechert fields and their asymptotic flux, which the run homes on the later mathematical page em-retarded-point-prerequisites (and the physics page em-retarded-fields-and-radiation); the present pair treats only smooth compactly supported volume sources and must not assume point-source regularity.

contents.name: §7.5.4 Causality and the Kramers-Kronig Relation (pp. 200-203): the polarisability as a response function, the time-domain turning-on argument for causality, the indented contour and the Kramers-Kronig pair for α(ω)
contents.support: An independent read-out of the causality-to-dispersion-relations route for the electric polarisability, corroborating the consumer's clauses (b)-(d) and the material-response motivation; the consumer keeps the purely mathematical statement and its exact hypotheses, and the example page records that neither the sign of the imaginary part nor positivity of the work follows from causality.

contents.name: §7.6 Conductors Revisited (Drude model and the dynamics of screening, p. 204 onwards)
contents.reason: The Drude conductor model is a specific material-response model with no consumer among this pair's items or the current run's planned pages; the pair's causal-response item is deliberately model-free, so declining this application removes no promised claim and adds no missing prerequisite.

sources.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Classical Electromagnetism (University of Texas at Austin lecture notes), chapter 'Retarded potentials' (node 50)
sources.locator: The complete node 'Retarded potentials' (node50.html), the section in 'Time-dependent Maxwell's equations' that solves the time-dependent Maxwell equations with the time-dependent Green's function and displays the retarded potential solutions (equations 508-510); the node's SI conventions are stated at its equations (504)-(510).

contents.name: The retarded potential solutions (node 50, equations 508-510): φ and A as the 1/(4πR) integrals of ρ and J evaluated at the retarded time, obtained from the time-dependent Green's function (499) and contrasted with the static Poisson solutions (504)-(505)
contents.support: An independent-author statement that the retarded potentials are given by exactly the 1/R retarded integrals used in clause (a) of the consumer; it corroborates the identification of the consumer's potentials with the wave-equation solution and confirms that no decay hypothesis on the source is used beyond the compact support built into the integral over the source region.

sources.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Classical Electromagnetism (University of Texas at Austin lecture notes), chapter 'Retarded fields' (node 52)
sources.locator: The complete node 'Retarded fields' (node52.html): differentiation of the retarded potentials with the identity (538)-(540) to obtain E and B, equations (541)-(542) described there as the time-dependent generalizations of Coulomb's and Biot-Savart laws, and the subsequent far-field discussion.

contents.name: The retarded field formulas (node 52, equations 541-542): E and B written as the exact retarded integrals of ρ, ρ_t and J, J_t with the 1/R² and 1/R kernels, obtained by differentiating the retarded potentials
contents.support: Corroborates the field-integral formulas of clause (a) of the consumer, which the consumer proves by differentiation under the integral sign on the region |x|>2a; the source also separates the 1/R² near-field terms from the 1/R terms whose fluxes survive at infinity, matching the consumer's separation of orders in clauses (b)-(c).

sources.title: P. Hadley, Advanced Solid State Physics (TU Graz), course note 'Causality and the Kramers-Kronig relations'
sources.locator: The complete course note: impulse response function and causality, generalized susceptibility as the Fourier transform of the impulse response, the even/odd decomposition of a causal kernel, the time-domain Kramers-Kronig relations, the frequency-domain principal-value relations, and the explicit warning about the sign convention for the imaginary part.

contents.name: Impulse response, causality and the generalized susceptibility: g(t)=0 for t<0, χ(ω)=∫g(t)e^{−iωt}dt, and the harmonic-response relation v(ω)=χ(ω)F(ω), together with the explicit statement that the imaginary part changes sign between the e^{iωt} and e^{−iωt} conventions
contents.support: Corroborates the consumer's clause (a) (causal kernel and its transform) and clause (d) (harmonic response and the imaginary part); it is the reason the consumer fixes its sign convention explicitly in clause (d), so that 'positive imaginary part' is stated relative to the e^{−iωt} phasor convention rather than left implicit.

contents.name: Kramers-Kronig in the time domain (even/odd decomposition and sign function) and in the frequency domain (principal-value integrals with the 1/(ω'±ω) kernels), with the applications list to susceptibility, conductivity and dielectric functions
contents.support: A second independent-author derivation of the same pair of principal-value dispersion relations proved in the consumer's clauses (b)-(c), by the time-domain even/odd route rather than by the indented contour; it supports the claim that the pair of formulas is the standard content of the causality-to-analyticity implication and confirms the sign normalisation used in the consumer.

canonical.name: The pair's own constructed theorem: causal convolution response on bounded continuous histories, its transfer function in the compact and integrable branches, the principal-value dispersion relations, and the monochromatic period-averaged work with its Hermitian-part positivity
canonical.support: Not a heading of any source: the pair's constructed statement assembles the recorded D1-D2 research argument (completed-expansion-arguments.md#D1-D2) with the passivity quadratic form, and gives it exact hypotheses (K∈L¹; compactly supported C^∞ kernels; locally absolutely continuous kernels with K,K',sK∈L¹), the exact reality identity, the exact |z|-bounds and the exact dispersion formulas, with the passivity equivalence stated as a mathematical equivalence rather than as a physical consequence.

canonical.name: The pair's own constructed theorem: uniform far-zone asymptotics and the fixed-retarded-time outward flux limit for smooth compact conserved sources, with the field-integral representation and the identification with the zero-data wave Cauchy solution
canonical.support: Not a heading of any source: the pair's constructed statement fixes the class of sources (smooth, spatially supported in B_a, temporally in [t_0,T], with ∂_vρ+div J=0), defines the retarded potentials and fields by explicit integrals, proves the uniform O(r^{-2}) errors with constants controlled by finitely many source suprema, the continuity identity ∫ρ_t=(n/c)·V, and the flux limit at fixed retarded time; the sources above supply the standard retarded-potential/retarded-field and dipole-radiation ingredients, not the exact uniform error statement.

canonical.name: The pair's own constructed example: the causal kernel K(s)=−e^{−s} with χ(ω)=−1/(1−iω) and Im χ(ω)<0, and the vanishing of the fixed-observation-time far-zone flux for large r
canonical.support: Not a heading of any source: clause (i) is the recorded example (mathematical-example-verifications.md) that a causal convolution can have a strictly negative imaginary part, so nonnegative period-averaged work is an additional passivity condition; clause (ii) was added by this scaffolder to exercise the second theorem's declared example dependency and to make its recorded fixed-retarded-time caveat checkable, and is proved by direct substitution into the field formulas.
